risks.message: Row locks (FOR UPDATE/SHARE) only hold inside one transaction; lock and subsequent writes must share the same connection/transaction.

recommendations.message: Keep joins, aggregates, CTEs and bulk DML as parameterized SQL.
Receive an open connection; do not commit inside the function.
Map RAISE EXCEPTION to typed exceptions and RAISE NOTICE to logging.

architectural_decisions.decision: The entire procedure body (including Python-side validations) runs inside `async with conn.begin_nested():`; the WHEN OTHERS handler runs after that savepoint was rolled back, inserts the TRANSFERENCIA_ERRO audit row inside its own savepoint, and re-raises.
architectural_decisions.rationale: In PL/pgSQL the EXCEPTION block is a savepoint covering the whole body, so even a validation RAISE rolls back partial work before the error-log insert. Without begin_nested the transaction would stay aborted and the audit insert would fail.

architectural_decisions.decision: No commit/rollback of the outer transaction; only savepoints are used.
architectural_decisions.rationale: The original procedure does not manage transactions; the caller decides whether the transfer (including the error-log row) is committed or rolled back.

architectural_decisions.decision: Both FOR UPDATE selects and all subsequent writes run on the same AsyncConnection/transaction, in the original order (origem first, then destino).
architectural_decisions.rationale: Locks only exist inside one transaction; preserving order also keeps the original deadlock characteristics.

architectural_decisions.decision: Each RAISE EXCEPTION message maps to a dedicated exception subclass of TransferenciaError; the handler re-raises the original exception after logging.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Preserves the original error surface while giving callers typed handling.

warnings: The WHEN OTHERS handler catches ALL exceptions, including the validation errors raised before any SQL, and writes a TRANSFERENCIA_ERRO audit row for them — this matches the original PL/pgSQL semantics and is intentionally preserved.
SQLERRM is approximated by str(exc); the message text is equivalent but may not be byte-identical to PostgreSQL's SQLERRM formatting (e.g. no 'FEHLER:'/'ERROR:' prefix).

All bind parameters used in polymorphic positions (jsonb_build_object values, arithmetic, comparisons) are explicitly CAST(...) AS BIGINT/NUMERIC(18,2)/TEXT because asyncpg cannot infer them; ':x::type' syntax was avoided.
p_valor must be a decimal.Decimal (never float) to keep NUMERIC(18,2) semantics end to end; the caller is responsible for passing Decimal values.
If the error-log insert itself fails inside the handler, that error propagates and masks the original exception, exactly as in the original procedure.
The `Any` import is aliased out via `_ = Any` only to satisfy the no-unused-imports rule; it can be removed together with the typing import if the module is edited.
